answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making standing earned, not bought: an identity gains weight only from a history of completed useful tasks whose outputs are publicly checkable and re-runnable, like a prism splitting one beam into many verifiable rays. Each task is drawn fresh, so a farm cannot copy one success across a thousand identities; and standing decays without new work, so every fake identity needs its own endless stream of real effort. A single onyx shard of reputation means little, but a summit built from years of checked work cannot be faked in bulk.
